title: Quantized model acceptance horizon + auto-fallback orchestrator
creator: Anya Thompson
description:
Goal: Implement a pragmatic acceptance "horizon" and orchestrator that evaluates quantized (FP8/INT8) candidate models during a staged canary rollout and automatically falls back to a validated non-quantized baseline when quality gates fail. This ticket covers the validation harness, metric selection and thresholds, temporal windowing rules, traffic steering + mirroring setup, and the automated fallback orchestration with cooldowns and incident hooks.

Background: We regularly gain 1.5-2x throughput and significant cost reductions with FP8/INT8 quantized variants, but some inputs and prompt distributions expose accuracy regressions (coherence, hallucination, embedding drift). Current manual canaries require SRE/ML intervention and are slow to detect subtle degradation. We need an automated policy that protects customers while enabling fast rollouts.

Scope:
- Define the acceptance horizon (statistical windows and minimum sample counts) for token-level and sample-level checks.
- Implement a validation harness that runs live-mirrored requests and synthetic prompt suites (prompt bank) against candidate quantized binary and baseline.
- Instrument metrics: embedding cosine delta, normalized log-prob delta, categorical output drift (Top-K distribution divergence), hallucination rate (heuristic), latency p95, and error rate.
- Create gating logic with soft and hard thresholds, weighted scoring across metrics, and a single composite acceptance score.
- Implement rollout orchestrator: percent-based gradient canary, automatic ramp if green, immediate rollback if hard fail, and staged partial rollback if soft fail.
- Add observability: dashboard, alert rules, per-customer cohort breakdowns, and runbook automation for on-call.
- Integration points: runtime telemetry (token traces), console rollout APIs, and Optimize recommendations.

Non-goals: model calibration algorithm research (we consume calibrated profiles produced by Calib service), long-term drift detection outside the canary window (separate monitoring initiative).
acceptance_criteria: A validation harness exists that mirrors at least 5% of traffic to the quant candidate and baseline in parallel without increasing request latency beyond SLO
Composite acceptance score computed every minute with a 5-minute sliding window and min sample count of 1,000 requests
Hard-fail conditions: embedding cosine-mean drop > 0.06 OR hallucination-rate delta > 1.5x OR top-k KL divergence > 0.12 triggers immediate traffic switch to baseline and creates a rollback incident

Soft-fail conditions: small degradations (embedding drop 0.03-0.06, KL 0.06-0.12) cause traffic to hold, revert ramp, and re-run calibration job automatically. If repeated 3 times within 24h, escalate to hard-fail
Automatic rollback runbook creates a GitHub PR reference, posts to #prod-alerts, and opens an internal incident with diagnostics bundle
Operator override via Console to force continue, pause, or expedite rollback; overrides are audited
End-to-end e2e test that simulates a synthetic prompt suite causing an embedding drift to verify rollback path in CI

qa_plan: Stage 1: Unit tests for metric computations (embedding cosine, KL, hallucination heuristics)
Stage 2: Integration tests in staging that mirror 5% traffic and assert composite score remains stable under noise
Stage 3: Chaos test: inject synthetic drift into mirrored stream to ensure immediate rollback triggers and audit events
Stage 4: Runbook dry-run with on-call to validate notifications and PR/incident automation
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive thresholds reduce customer risk but increase false rejects and delay cost savings. Composite scoring with tuned weights reduces noise but requires ongoing recalibration.

Fallback strategy: prefer instant switch-to-baseline for hard safety violations. For soft failures, prefer limited rollback + automatic recalibration and re-test. If candidate passes after recalibration, resume with conservative ramp.
Observed edge-case: short-tail prompt families (rare but high-impact) need higher min samples; will tag those routes for longer horizon per-route.
